ceiling.declared_bases.meaning: the bases written in the class statement; bases added at runtime are not included, and bases that don't resolve to exactly one class are listed in unresolved_superclasses, an ambiguous base (imported by a try/except shim, or rebound by an if/else) among them (#1057)

ceiling.literal_subclassing.meaning: project classes whose class statement names this class as a base, resolved as superclasses resolves it: a class whose base is ambiguous (imported by a try/except shim, or rebound by an if/else) is not listed under any of its candidates (#1057). Classes built with type(), class factories or __init_subclass__ registration are not included. The scan skips virtual environments (a directory holding pyvenv.cfg, whatever its name) and directories named like caches or build output (build, dist, env, venv, .tox and the like) unless they hold __init__.py or __init__.pyi; a PEP 420 namespace package with such a name is not scanned (#1104)

ceiling.on_disk_modules.meaning: modules and subpackages present on disk under the package; entries added to __path__ at runtime are not included

ceiling.package_reexports.meaning: import bindings written in source in the public modules of the symbol's own package (#712); re-exports from other packages and names provided lazily by a module __getattr__ are not included

ceiling.static_calls.meaning: calls whose target static analysis resolves; dynamic calls are counted in unresolved_call_sites, not listed

ceiling.static_definitions.meaning: definitions written in source: a class body (methods, nested classes, class-level assignments) or a module's top level. Instance attributes assigned in methods (self.x = ...) and anything injected at runtime (metaclass, setattr, __getattr__, type(), __init_subclass__) are not included

ceiling.static_imports.meaning: import statements written in source; importlib / __import__ with a computed name is not included. A stub's (.pyi) own imports are declarations, not runtime imports: imported_by doesn't count them, while imports on a stub module lists them (#933). For imported_by, the scan skips virtual environments (a directory holding pyvenv.cfg, whatever its name) and directories named like caches or build output (build, dist, env, venv, .tox and the like) unless they hold __init__.py or __init__.pyi; a PEP 420 namespace package with such a name is not scanned (#1104)

determinism.ast.meaning: read from the syntax tree of the project's files, without calling Jedi; the same result in every process for the same source

determinism.filesystem.meaning: read from a directory listing, without calling Jedi; the same result in every process for the same files on disk

determinism.goto.meaning: each adjacent is a Jedi forward goto target. Project-scope adjacents are the same in every process; an external (stdlib or installed) target behind a try/except import shim may differ between processes (#419), so don't compare external adjacents across sessions. A name bound to more than one target (a base imported by a try/except shim, or rebound by an if/else) resolves to none, never to a pick (#1057)

determinism.jedi_local.meaning: read by Jedi from the source's own file, with no cross-file inference; the same result in every process for the same source

env.PYEYE_ISSUE.deprecated: accepted and ignored; nothing records sessions any more (#943)

env.PYEYE_PARENT_SESSION.deprecated: accepted and ignored; nothing records sessions any more (#943)

resolver.bare_name.exact_module.summary: a complete top-level module (the project's package, a namespace root or an external module) wins over same-named definitions

resolver.bare_name.members.summary: only when nothing above matched, every method or class attribute with that name, decided the same way; dunder names never match

resolver.bare_name.name_index.summary: every project definition with that name, canonicalised: one is the answer, several are ambiguous

resolver.bare_name.shadow.summary: a top-level package or module under more than one project root is ambiguous

resolver.strategy.definition_placement.summary: the definition in the deepest project module along the path, following a re-export alias to its definition (an explicit import, or a `from x import *` of a name x star-exports), with no fallback to shallower modules

resolver.strategy.external_definition.summary: a definition at exactly the requested path, found by goto

resolver.strategy.external_module.summary: a stdlib or site-packages module, through a Jedi import

resolver.strategy.guarded_inference.summary: an inferred definition, accepted only if its name equals the last component

resolver.strategy.namespace_package.summary: a PEP 420 namespace package: a directory with importable content and no init file

resolver.strategy.private_stdlib.summary: a stdlib definition in a private module, named by its public re-exporting module

resolver.strategy.project_module.summary: a project module, as a package or a single file

review.axis.cross_cutting.description: Cross-cutting access: logging, config, path handling.

review.axis.dependency_acquisition.description: Dependency acquisition: constructor-injection vs import vs global/singleton.

review.axis.error_handling.description: Error handling: raise vs return-sentinel vs result-type; exception types; where caught.

review.axis.layering.description: Layering / dependency direction: which layers/packages may import which.

review.axis.module_boundaries.description: Module & placement boundaries: where a *kind* of thing lives.

review.axis.naming_api_shape.description: Naming & API shape: naming patterns, return-type conventions, sync/async split.

review.axis.validation_placement.description: Validation placement: at the boundary vs in core vs scattered.

scope.option.all.meaning: the main project, every configured package and namespace, and the standalone directories

scope.option.namespace.meaning: one namespace's package directories; namespace:a.b resolves under namespace a

scope.option.package.meaning: that directory, if it exists: an absolute path, or one relative to the project (project_path)

scope.option.standalone.meaning: the standalone script directories: those in the config's standalone.dirs, for scripts that aren't in any package

facts.security.path_checks.forms: the deny-list checks the target's lexical and resolved forms.
